Sampled ranking can conceal catalog-level failures: [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show that sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation; small candidate sets increasingly resemble AUC rather than top-heavy ranking. A [sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045) finds that both uniform and popularity-based candidate sampling can disagree with full-catalog rankings. The 2025 study [On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) examines resolution, fidelity, robustness and predictive power under different sampling and exposure policies. Repeating candidate draws measures sampling variability; it does not eliminate systematic sampling bias.

Popularity and repetition warrant separate diagnostics. [Negative-sampling experiments from 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) report that random negative sampling reinforces popularity bias and favors head items. [Repetition and Exploration in Sequential Recommendation](https://staff.fnwi.uva.nl/m.derijke/wp-content/papercite-data/pdf/li-2023-repetition.pdf) identifies repetitive bias, including effects from shared input/output item embeddings. These findings support checking whether apparently strong pairwise margins coexist with weak rankings against competitive items, particularly for rare or novel targets.

Suggested diagnostic design, inferred from this evidence: score catalog items in chunks for selected training prefixes, reporting target rank and the number of eligible items scoring above it; exclude padding and future interactions from the prefix. For repeat targets, retain the target when applying history exclusions. Repeat draws of 99 unique negatives and report rank quantiles and hit-frequency variation. Stratify results by training-only item frequency, prefix length and target presence in the prefix, with group counts. Treat these as training-fit and sampling-sensitivity probes, not generalization estimates; keep them separate from pinned host validation HR@10.
